newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean won ends little changed on intervention.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean won ends little changed on intervention.

text.p: The won closed barely changed versus the dollar on Tuesday after plunging to a low of 829.80 as the central bank came to a quick rescue, dealers said.
They said the central bank intervened a couple of times in the afternoon but failed to overturn won's decline led by huge import settlements and dollar short-covering.
The central bank denied the intervention as it always does.
The won closed at 828.80, the all-time low close level same as on Monday. It opened at 829.00. But dealers forecast Wednesday's mid-rate at 828.80 against 827.30 today.
Traders said the interventions are the only support for the falling won in a market that is severely short of dollars.

"The dollar is expected to rise on Wednesday and could hit another all-time high," said a local bank trader. "Banks will buy dollars to settle expected import deals towards the weekend and to cover their short dollar positions."
Dealers expect the won to move in a range of 828.00 to 832.00 on Wednesday.
